subject: Discovery: compatibility check-in — NovaMed LLM migration next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T15:02:00Z
Subject: Discovery: compatibility check-in — NovaMed LLM migration next steps

Hi Lucy — thanks again for the intro call earlier today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of pain points you called out:
- Token/usage cost with current OpenAI usage is driving >60% of query cost for search & summarization flows.
- Rate-limiting and per-request throttling during peak hours causing user-facing timeouts.
- Vendor lock-in concerns: procurement wants an exit path that preserves behavioral parity for key prompts.
- Compliance: certain PHI-handling paths must remain in a VPC/on-prem environment and require audit logs and KMS integration.

Current stack (from call):
- Generation + chat: OpenAI (GPT-4 variant) for conversational flows.
- Summarization / classification: Anthropic Claude for few-shot summarization.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings; custom post-processing pipeline running in AWS Fargate.
- Daily inference: ~1.2M tokens/day, ~80 RPS peak in the east coast region.

Success criteria you gave us:
- Output quality parity within ±5% on our evaluation metrics (ROUGE/BERTScore + manual QA for critical prompts).
- 95th percentile latency < 300ms for single-turn token-limited requests (interactive product flows).
- Unit cost reduction target: ~40% on a per-token basis (including infra).
- Security: SOC 2 evidence, VPC/private deployment option, and KMS/HSM key control.

Open model shortlist (preliminary, for discussion):
- Llama 3 (quantized variants) — good middle ground for cost & quality on chat.
- Mistral-instruct (larger param, strong instruction tuning behavior).
- Falcon-instruct (as a candidate for heavy hallucination-resistant outputs).
(we'll do evals on the shortlist and extend if needed).

Deliverables & next steps (owners / ETA):
1) Compatibility matrix (owner: Jonas) — mapping of current API patterns, prompt surfaces, tokenization/embedding formats, and KV cache expectations. Attached: compatibility-matrix.xlsx. — ETA: 2026-09-14
2) Technical deep-dive w/ engineering + your infra/procurement (owner: Marissa) — agenda below. Proposed slots: Tue 2026-09-15 or Wed 2026-09-16. Please confirm availability.
3) Provide a small sample of prompts + anonymized dataset for us to run quick parity evals (owner: NovaMed) — ETA: before deep-dive preferred.
4) Procurement checklist & SOC2 evidence link (owner: Jonas) — I'll include SOC2 link and a short risk matrix in the HubSpot record.

Quick meeting agenda we suggest for the deep-dive:
- 15m: Architecture & traffic patterns (NovaMed infra)
- 20m: Compatibility risks (tokenization, response schema, streaming, function-calls)
- 20m: Migration plan options (hosted fallback, dedicated capacity, private deployment)
- 15m: Procurement questions & next steps

If that aligns with you, I'll circulate the invite and upload the initial compatibility matrix + shortlist results to the Drive link below.

Drive (shared): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-novamed-evals
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/RDW-2026-0453

Attachment: compatibility-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 28KB)

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
